title: Fractals in Jackson Pollock's paintings

plain: The drip paintings of the American artist Jackson Pollock, made from the late 1940s on, are said to contain fractals, patterns that repeat the same shape at smaller and smaller scales, as found in nature. The philosopher Jason Jorjani raises this, telling the host to "go look this up" in a Scientific American magazine article called "Order in Pollock's Chaos," by the physicist Richard P. Taylor, and he also points to his own book Lovers of Sophia. He uses it to suggest that Pollock tapped into a hidden natural order without knowing it.
